slides.0.title: Oregon I: the Willamette Valley
slides.0.subtitle: Overview and sub-AVAs
slides.1.title: The parent AVA and its climate
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Extent
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Bounded by the Coast Range to the west, the Cascades to the east, the Columbia River to the north and the Calapooya Mountains to the south; the parent AVA was approved by the ATF at the end of 1983 (some sources say 1984)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Climate
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Latitude about 45 degrees north; about 40 inches of rain a year, mostly October to May; summer afternoons are typically 75 to 85°F
slides.1.highlights.2.title: The Van Duzer Corridor
slides.1.highlights.2.content: A gap in the Coast Range that lets Pacific air into the valley on summer afternoons and evenings and cools it
slides.1.content: The Willamette Valley is a cool, damp valley ringed by mountains, with the Van Duzer gap supplying summer sea air.
slides.2.title: The eleven sub-AVAs
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Eleven as of 2022
slides.2.highlights.0.content: In order of approval: Dundee Hills and Yamhill-Carlton District (2004), McMinnville and Ribbon Ridge (2005), Chehalem Mountains and Eola-Amity Hills (around 2006), Van Duzer Corridor (2018 or 2019), Tualatin Hills and Laurelwood District (2020), Lower Long Tom (2021) and Mount Pisgah, Polk County (2022)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Elevation ranges
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Vineyards in Yamhill-Carlton, McMinnville and Tualatin Hills are limited to 200 to 1,000 feet
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Rain shadow
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Yamhill-Carlton lies in the rain shadow of the roughly 3,500-foot Coast Range
slides.2.content: Do not memorise every year; remember two batches: the original six of 2004–2006 and the additions after 2018.
slides.3.title: Vintage variation
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Cool years
slides.3.highlights.0.content: 2010 was described as Oregon's coolest season in 30 years; 2011 was the latest and coldest on record
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Hot years
slides.3.highlights.1.content: 2014 had record heat and a big crop, all picked by 1 October; 2015 was described as Oregon's hottest year on record
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Effect on style
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Cool years lean towards high acidity and lower alcohol; hot years give riper fruit and alcohol near 14%
slides.3.content: Willamette vintages vary widely, which makes them a good example when discussing vintage in D3 tasting and essays.
